bio: Peter Karl Oberacker Jr. (born May 13, 1963) is an American businessman and politician. He is a member of the New York State Senate representing the 51st district. The boundaries of the 51st district changed following the 2020 United States redistricting cycle, and the district now includes portions of Broome, Chenango, Delaware, Otsego, Schoharie, Sullivan, and Ulster counties.
offices: Member of the State Senate of New York (2021–present)

items.t: Co-sponsored the bipartisan New York Food Safety and Chemical Disclosure Act, which would ban certain food additives and require additive disclosure by packaged food companies.
items.q: Oberacker co-sponsored the bipartisan "New York Food Safety and Chemical Disclosure Act," which would ban certain food additives and colorants, and require packaged food companies to disclose more detailed information

items.t: Called for a state Senate investigation into the practices of utility companies such as NYSEG (2025).
items.q: Oberacker called on the New York State Senate Investigations and Government Operations Committee to launch a full-scale investigation into the practices of utility companies

items.t: Introduced the "Ratepayer Bill of Rights," legislation outlining rights for utility customers, from accurate billing to fair outage compensation.
items.q: Oberacker has also introduced the "Ratepayer Bill of Rights", a series of legislation that would outline "fundamental rights that utility customers should be guaranteed from accurate billing to fair outage compensation."

items.t: Voted against the bill that legalized recreational cannabis in New York (2021).
items.q: Oberacker voted against the bill that legalized recreational cannabis in New York.

items.t: Sponsored a bill designating baseball as New York's official state sport; it passed the Senate 61–2.
items.q: Oberacker's first bill to be approved by the senate was a bill that designated baseball as the official state sport of New York
